title: The Happy Prince and Other Tales
author: Oscar Wilde
short_summary: This 1888 collection gathers several of Oscar Wilde's best-loved fairy tales, including 'The Happy Prince,' 'The Nightingale and the Rose,' 'The Selfish Giant,' 'The Devoted Friend,' and 'The Remarkable Rocket.' Each story uses beauty, sacrifice, and gentle irony to explore what it truly means to be kind and generous.
extended_summary:
In 'The Happy Prince,' a golden statue overlooking a city asks a little swallow to help him give away his jewels and gold leaf to the poor people he can see suffering below, even though it costs the swallow its chance to fly south before winter. In 'The Nightingale and the Rose,' a nightingale sacrifices her own life, pressing her heart against a thorn, to create a red rose so that a heartbroken student can win his love — only for the gift to be carelessly tossed aside. 'The Selfish Giant' tells of a giant who builds a wall around his beautiful garden to keep children out, only to discover that without children, spring never comes to his garden at all.

The collection also includes 'The Devoted Friend,' a story about a small, honest man taken advantage of by a wealthier 'friend' who mistakes selfishness for devotion, and 'The Remarkable Rocket,' a comic tale about a firework so proud of himself that he fails to notice the world around him. Together, these tales use fantasy and fable to gently teach lessons about generosity, sacrifice, and true friendship, often through beauty that comes at a cost and characters who learn — sometimes too late — what really matters.

questions.prompt: In 'The Happy Prince,' what does the statue ask the swallow to help him do?

options: Give away his jewels and gold leaf to help the poor
Fly south for the winter with him
Build a nest in the town square
Guard the city from thieves

questions.explanation: The Happy Prince statue asks the swallow to carry his jewels and gold leaf, piece by piece, to people suffering in the city below.

questions.prompt: What does the swallow give up by staying to help the Happy Prince?

options: His chance to fly south before winter arrives
His ability to sing
His friendship with other birds
His home in Egypt

questions.explanation: By staying to help the Prince give away his riches, the swallow delays his migration south and eventually cannot survive the cold.

questions.prompt: In 'The Nightingale and the Rose,' how does the nightingale create a red rose?

options: By pressing her heart against a thorn and singing through the night
By painting a white rose red with berry juice
By asking a wizard for a magic spell
By watering a rosebush with her own tears

questions.explanation: The nightingale sacrifices her life, pressing her heart to a thorn as she sings, so that her blood colors the rose red.

questions.prompt: What happens to the red rose the nightingale dies to create?

options: The student is rejected anyway and carelessly tosses the rose into the gutter
The girl marries the student out of gratitude
The rose becomes famous throughout the kingdom
The rose is planted and grows into a whole garden

questions.explanation: In a bitterly ironic twist, the girl the student loves rejects him regardless, and he throws the precious rose away without realizing its cost.

questions.prompt: Why does the Selfish Giant build a wall around his garden?

options: To keep children from playing in it
To protect it from a storm
To hide treasure buried inside
To keep other giants out

questions.explanation: The Giant builds the wall selfishly to stop children from enjoying his garden, wanting to keep its beauty only for himself.

questions.prompt: What happens to the Giant's garden after he shuts the children out?

options: Spring never comes, and the garden stays locked in winter
The garden grows even more beautiful than before
The garden disappears completely
Other giants come to admire it

questions.explanation: Without the children's laughter and presence, the garden is stuck in endless winter, showing how the Giant's selfishness harms even himself.

questions.prompt: In 'The Selfish Giant,' the garden only becomes beautiful again once the Giant lets the ___ back in.
questions.explanation: Spring only returns to the garden once the Giant tears down the wall and welcomes the children back.

questions.prompt: Sort each act into the correct group.

content.groupA: An act of generosity or sacrifice

options.label: The Happy Prince gives away his jewels to help the poor
The nightingale gives her life to create a red rose
The Giant builds a wall to keep children out
The student throws away the rose without a second thought

questions.explanation: These tales contrast selfless sacrifice — like the Prince's and the nightingale's — with careless selfishness, like the Giant's wall and the student's indifference.

questions.prompt: Match each story with its central character.

right: A golden statue who gives away his riches
A bird who sacrifices herself for love's sake
A giant who learns to share his garden
A poor, honest man taken advantage of by a false friend

questions.explanation: Each story centers on a different character whose choices reveal Wilde's themes of generosity, sacrifice, and true versus false friendship.

questions.prompt: Put these events from 'The Happy Prince' in the order they happen.

items: A swallow stops to rest at the feet of the Happy Prince's statue
The Prince asks the swallow to give away his jewels and gold leaf
The swallow stays through the winter to keep helping, growing weaker
The swallow dies, and the Prince's leaden heart breaks

questions.explanation: This traces the story's arc from the swallow's arrival through his sacrifice and its sorrowful, tender ending.

questions.prompt: In 'The Devoted Friend,' the rich man calls himself the poor man's best friend, but takes far more than he gives. Do you think he is a true friend? Why or why not?
questions.explanation: There is no single correct answer — the story invites readers to examine the difference between one-sided taking and genuine, mutual friendship.

questions.prompt: What is 'The Remarkable Rocket' mainly about?

options: A firework who is so proud of himself that he ignores everyone around him
A prince who searches for a magical rocket
A scientist who invents fireworks for a festival
A bird who wishes she could fly like a rocket

questions.explanation: The story comically follows a vain firework who talks endlessly about his own importance, missing the celebration happening around him.

questions.prompt: If you could give away one prized possession to help someone in need, the way the Happy Prince does, what would it be and why?
questions.explanation: This encourages children to connect the collection's theme of generous sacrifice to their own imagination and values.

questions.prompt: What common theme runs through most of the stories in this collection?

options: True beauty and goodness often involve sacrifice and giving to others
Wealth always brings happiness
Selfishness is usually rewarded
Animals and objects cannot show real feelings

questions.explanation: Across the collection, characters who sacrifice for others — the Prince, the swallow, the nightingale, the Giant once he changes — embody Wilde's recurring theme that true beauty is bound up with generosity and sacrifice.
